references.text: The Levites received cities to live in from the other tribes, since they did not receive any territory as an inheritance. This explains the background for the Levites' special property rights.
Describes the distribution of the Levitical cities among the tribes of Israel, which is the concrete implementation of the laws concerning the Levites' dwellings and properties.
Continuation of the law regarding the Levites' right of redemption, clarifying that their houses can always be redeemed and that the fields surrounding the cities cannot be sold.
Explains why the Levites had special property rules: they received no inheritance share in the land because the Lord himself was their inheritance and portion.
Confirms that the Levites were to have no inheritance share among Israel, but were to live from the Lord's offerings.
The prophet Ezekiel confirms the principle that the Levites' land must not be sold or exchanged, because it is dedicated to the Lord.
